title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows, optimize deps & cache hygiene
author: Ari Patel
description: Motivation: our repo contains a number of duplicated CI workflows across packages and services which increases maintenance surface and slows iteration when updating actions or cache policies. This change consolidates lint, test, and release orchestration into a smaller set of reusable workflows and composite actions, upgrades core actions and node toolchains, and tightens cache keys to reduce stale cache misses. Goals: 1) unify lint/test/release entrypoints to reduce duplication and drift; 2) upgrade actions and node tool versions for security and speed; 3) reduce CI runtime by improving cache hit rates and parallelism; 4) keep release automation behavior unchanged for consumers. Changes included: - Introduce .github/actions/ci-composite/* composite actions for shared steps (checkout, setup-node, install-cache, report) and reuse them from package-specific workflows - Consolidate previous .github/workflows/{lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml} across services into three centralized workflows with targeted job matrices to avoid running irrelevant suites on unrelated changes - Upgrade actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 and pin to minor versions to avoid unexpected breaking changes - Add deterministic cache keys including repo-specific + lockfile digest + node-version to reduce cross-branch pollution; add separate caches for deps and build artifacts - Replace custom cache restore logic in a couple of legacy workflows with the shared composite action - Simplify the matrix for JS/TS packages to run lint once per changed package path and run tests in parallel where appropriate - Tweak release workflow: keep the existing GHA dispatch interface and changelog parsing but move common upload and publish steps into composite to make future auth changes easier - Add a short-lived E2E gating job that is opt-in on feature branches and required for release/* merges - Update root package.json devDeps (eslint, jest, typescript) to latest safe minors and regenerate lockfile - Add CI health dashboard telemetry tags to all workflows for easier alerting in the console Checklist: - [x] Migrate duplicated steps into composite actions - [x] Upgrade core actions and pin versions - [x] Improve cache key hygiene and separate caches - [x] Reduce redundant matrix paralellism - [x] Run CI end-to-end locally via act and spot-check windows runner - [x] Add telemetry tags - [x] Preserve release automation behavior and tags Testing performed: ran workflows in fork with synthetic changes, verified cache hits improved from ~42% to ~79% in sampling, observed median lint/test workflow time reduce ~23%, reran release workflow with dry-run publish to staging registry, validated that canary release still behaves the same as before Notes: this is a refactor focused on developer experience and maintenance; no product behavior changes expected. If issues arise, rollback by reverting to the previous workflow files which are retained in the branch history.

release_notes:
- Consolidated CI workflows and introduced reusable composite actions for checkout/setup/install/report
- Upgraded core GH actions and bumped devDependencies (eslint, jest, typescript)
- Improved caching keys and separated build/dependency caches to increase hit rate and reduce runtime
- Added optional E2E gating job and telemetry tags for CI health
